doc.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Spirituality and cultural background in her music
summary: Brown asks about Ellington's spirituality; she says what she observes shapes her.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Well, the pieces you mentioned—as you stated earlier—you are a socially conscious person, it‟s reflected in the music, particularly in the titles you just said were important to you. [Takes deep breath] When I look at Duke Ellington, yes, as we talked earlier, he was very much influenced by his cultural, uh, background. But also, Duke Ellington had a very strong spirituality, particularly in his later period.
So, for me that means humanity. Uh, spirituality means humanity.

So I see that in your music, as well. Do you feel that there‟s any kind of cultural influence in this consciousness of yours? You mentioned Buddha before; do you feel that Japanese culture or maybe just your early upbringing has had an impact on the way you view the world?

I would like to, I would like to think it does. I was mentioning earlier, that anything you observe—it doesn‟t necessarily have to be music—but it could be anything you observe and you felt something, right there you are influenced by [it]. So, that includes everything: political scene, government, policymaking, and social issues, what have you. So I would like to think my music will have all that, you know, digested in myself and comes out. I would like to think that.
Well, I think your music speaks that, so….
